title: AST/ALT ratio does not establish incremental prediction of older-adult grip strength across separate NHANES samples
abstract: Adding AST/ALT ratio to a flexible demographic/body-size/individual-enzyme baseline did not establish improved combined-grip prediction in 1,228 NHANES 2013–14 adults aged 60–79: weighted MSE gain 0.3525 kg² (conditional-source 95% target-PSU bootstrap interval -0.7539 to 1.3646). Frozen models trained in 1,076 NHANES 2011–12 adults were evaluated without refitting in 1,228 separately sampled 2013–14 adults. A stronger enzyme-interaction comparator reversed the small gain. This is a negative cross-sectional feature-engineering experiment, not clinical equivalence or sarcopenia diagnosis.
